chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in the Muhrim (person in Ihram) wrapping his head due to headache."
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And he does not cover himself (with a canopy/veil) unless he fears great harm.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (consecration)
key_terms.يُظَلِّلُ: To cover with a canopy or veil (distinct from wrapping)
key_terms.يُعَصِّبَ: To wrap or bind (specifically the head)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a Muhrim covering their head during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the permissibility of a muhrim covering their head specifically to relieve a headache, illustrating the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) within the strictures of Ihram. Shaykh al-Tusi’s appended note clarifies that this permission is not absolute but contingent upon the presence of significant harm or necessity, reflecting the Shia juristic approach of balancing ritual purity with physical well-being.
